patient_information: A 51-year-old female Swiss traveller, with no reported chronic underlying disease or medication intake.
chief_complaint: Generalized slightly pruritic maculopapular rash, non-purulent bilateral conjunctivitis, and peripheral oedema.
history_of_present_illness: Six days after returning from a 2-week holiday to Guatemala and El Salvador, the patient presented; four days after return, she noticed a generalized slightly pruritic maculopapular rash on the face, trunk, and extremities, without fever or other accompanying symptoms, and the next day the rash worsened and non-purulent bilateral conjunctivitis developed.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Returned from a 2-week holiday to Guatemala and El Salvador, regions where dengue, chikungunya, and zika are important arboviral infections.
physical_exam: Conjunctivitis, a generalised maculopapular rash involving the face, tender oedema of the hands, elbows, knees, and feet, and generalized lymphadenopathy (cervical, axillary, and inguinal).
labs_and_diagnostics: Full blood count was normal. CRP was 8 mg/L (>5) and creatinine was very mildly elevated (87 µmol/L, range 35-80 µmol/L); liver function tests were normal. Rapid diagnostic tests for dengue and chikungunya were negative. Zika virus infection was confirmed by PCR and seroconversion, with Zika IgM IIFT increasing from negative to 1:640, Zika IgG IIFT increasing from 1:20 to 1:5120, and Zika RT-PCR positive.
differential_diagnosis: Arboviral infection, specifically dengue, chikungunya, or zika.
management_and_clinical_course: Arboviral infections are self-limiting and, in the absence of specific treatment options, clinical management is exclusively supportive.
